text.title: Growth Experiment Design Worked Example
text.summary: One complete experiment spec for an e-commerce checkout change (trust badges under the card form: 4.2 percent baseline, 5 percent minimum effect, 143,000 per variant over three weeks, Statsig assignment on user_id, playback on a one-percent cohort, SRM p 0.41, shipped with a written-up 6.8 percent lift) with a note on each value, plus the same idea written the way growth teams usually write it and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A web shop with about 15,000 first-time checkout visitors a day converts 4.2 percent of them from the card form to a paid order. Exit surveys mention payment security. The growth team wants to show payment-provider trust badges under the card form. Statsig is the flag platform; events land in BigQuery.

example.title: exp-checkout-trust-badges
example.note: `minimum_effect_pct` 5 is a relative lift on a 4.2 percent rate, so the absolute change to detect is 0.21 points; at alpha 0.05 and power 0.8 that needs about 143,000 users per variant (r-sample-size-computed-before-launch). With 15,000 eligible users a day split 50/50, each arm collects 7,500 a day, so 143,000 takes 19.1 days, rounded up to 3 whole weeks; `stop_date` is exactly 21 days after `launch_date` (r-fixed-stop-date-no-peeking-srm-check). Confidence 6 is allowed because it cites a prior test and survey counts; without them it would be capped at 3 (r-ice-scored-before-build). The exposure event is the card form view, not the Statsig assignment, so users who never reach checkout do not dilute the lift (r-instrumentation-playback-before-ramp). `average order value` guards against badges nudging cheaper baskets, `repeat purchase` against a one-off effect, and page timing against the badge assets slowing checkout (r-one-primary-metric-plus-guardrails). SRM p 0.41 means the 50/50 split held; the write-up on 2026-03-30 is five days after the stop date, the 6.8 percent lift clears the 5 percent minimum with the whole confidence interval above zero, and no guardrail is breached, so `ship` is a legitimate decision (r-write-up-every-experiment).

example.title: the same idea as usually written
example.note: What the validator prints: `hypothesis.primary_metric` "engagement" is a theme and `minimum_effect_pct` 0 is not above zero (r-hypothesis-falsifiable-with-effect-size); one guardrail where three categories are required (r-one-primary-metric-plus-guardrails); `ice.confidence` 8 with no evidence cited (r-ice-scored-before-build); `alpha` 0.1 is not 0.05 and `duration_weeks` 10 is above 8 (r-sample-size-computed-before-launch); `design` pre_post, `hash_key` session_id and a single 100 percent allocation with no control (r-control-group-randomised-by-flag); `exposure_logged_at` assignment (r-instrumentation-playback-before-ramp); `counts_toward_velocity` true with no write-up (r-write-up-every-experiment). Once the schema violations are fixed the cross-field checks add: `status` running with a pending playback, and `stop_date` four days after launch where the duration demands whole weeks.
